title: How Sweet, upon This Sacred Day
description: How Sweet, upon This Sacred Day in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Eliza Lee Cabot Follen wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 9 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Love of Sabbath Service”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: How sweet, up-on this sa-cred day, The best of all the seven, To cast our earth-ly thoughts a-way, And think of God and heaven!

lines: How sweet, upon this sacred day,
The best of all the seven,
To cast our earthly thoughts away,
And think of God and heaven!
How sweet to be allowed to pray
How sweet the words of peace to hear
And lead the way to heaven!
And if, to make our sins depart,
In vain the will has striven,
He who regards the inmost heart
Will send his grace from heaven.

licence: Public domain: Eliza Lee Cabot Follen died in 1860.
credits: Words by Eliza Lee Cabot Follen (1787–1860), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
